evals.prompt: pick up the next auto-dev issue and build it, open a PR but don't merge
evals.expected_output: Selects the lowest-numbered ready auto-dev issue via auto_issue_dev.sh next-issue, branches with the issue-number prefix, implements test-first, verifies, and opens a (non-draft) PR that the #345 hook links with Closes #N. Stops at PR-open; never merges.

evals.prompt: run the autonomous issue developer until there's nothing left in the queue
evals.expected_output: Explains it develops one issue per invocation and is driven unattended via /loop /issue-dev-auto, terminating when next-issue exits 3 (empty queue), reporting how many issues were skipped as dependency-blocked.

evals.prompt: auto-develop issue work but if something has an unmerged dependency, don't touch it
evals.expected_output: Notes that next-issue auto-detects unmet dependencies (depends on/blocked by/requires/needs #M), tags those issues blocked-dependency, comments naming the blocker, and excludes them from the loop scope rather than developing them.

evals.prompt: after the PR is open, keep an eye on it — fix any review comments and failing checks, then merge it once everything's green
evals.expected_output: Runs the PR monitoring loop: pr_merge_loop.sh signals | merge_decision.sh decide; on `revise` runs /pr-address-comments,/project-verify,/pr-review (≤3 cycles); only merges on `merge` (CI green, no actionable human comment, /pr-review=merge, /project-verify pass, #360 gate Tier-1 pass, consensus≥0.80) via admin bypass; anything short → ready-to-merge/needs-human. Honors PR_MERGE_LOOP_APPLY (dry-run by default).

evals.prompt: run the whole auto-dev loop unattended and stop it when there's nothing left to do
evals.expected_output: Self-paced loop with a 10-min per-run ceiling; processes work one merge at a time (loop_lock); resets the empty-run counter on any work or in-flight PR and stops after 5 consecutive empty runs; halts entirely if a merge turns main CI red.

evals.prompt: is it safe to let this thing merge to main on its own?
evals.expected_output: Explains the fail-closed safety model: merge is opt-in (PR_MERGE_LOOP_APPLY=1), gated by a unit-tested decision (merge_decision.sh, SC-002 invariant) plus the #360 verification gate with BLOCKING consensus; no admin / conflict / red-main / infra failure ever produces a merge — those route to a human.
